chapters.title: Chapter 4: The Cost of Getting It Wrong

lessons.title: Paid Too Much? Refunds and Interest on Refunds

body.text: Overpaying tax is not a loss, but it is not a savings account either. Excess TDS or advance tax comes back as a refund once your return is processed, with interest of 0.5% a month that usually starts only on 1 April after the tax year. File on time, keep your bank account validated, and treat a refund as your own money returned late, not a bonus.

children.text: The first two lessons of this chapter covered the cost of paying too little. This one covers the opposite. Refunds are common among advance taxpayers: estimates run high, clients deduct more TDS than the final tax, or income falls after you have paid. Knowing how refunds and refund interest work helps you decide how cautious your estimates should really be.

body.caption: Any positive figure is refundable once your return is processed

markDefs.definition: An income tax return filed after the due date for that tax year. It is still valid, but carries a late fee, interest on any unpaid tax, and reduced refund interest.

children.text: The interest the department pays on refunds (old section 244A of the 1961 Act, carried into the 2025 Act) is simple interest. For refunds arising from TDS, TCS or advance tax, it runs from 1 April following the tax year until the refund is granted, but only if you file your return on time. For a
, it runs only from the date of filing.

body.title: Quick Check: Does the Refund Earn Interest?
body.question: Leela, a Bhubaneswar-based tutor, overpaid by ₹4,000. Her tax for the year, as determined when her return is processed, is ₹60,000. She filed on time and the refund arrives in August. How much interest does she get on the refund?
options: Nil, because the refund is less than 10% of her tax
Nil, because refunds never carry interest
body.explanation: 10% of ₹60,000 is ₹6,000, and her refund of ₹4,000 is below that, so no interest is payable on it. The refund itself is still paid in full. Refunds of 10% or more of tax do earn interest at 0.5% a month.

children.text: In Chapter 2, Dr Anand, the Lucknow consultant physician, had ₹4,00,000 of TDS deducted by hospitals against tax of ₹2,08,000 under the presumptive scheme. He paid no advance tax, filed his return on 20 July 2027, e-verified it the same day, and his refund was credited on 25 September 2027.

children.text: Refund interest is taxable as income from other sources in the year he receives it. At his 25% marginal slab plus cess, about ₹1,498 of the ₹5,760 goes back as tax.

events.title: Pre-validate your bank account
events.description: On the e-filing portal, under My Bank Account, add and pre-validate the account the refund should go to. Refunds are paid only to pre-validated accounts.

events.title: File the return
events.description: Claim all TDS, TCS and advance tax. Filing on time keeps refund interest running from 1 April.

events.title: e-Verify
events.description: A return is not treated as filed until it is verified, so verify immediately with Aadhaar OTP or net banking.

events.title: Processing and intimation
events.description: The Centralised Processing Centre processes the return and sends an intimation showing tax, interest and refund due.

events.title: Refund credited
events.description: Refund and interest are credited to the pre-validated account. Track progress through the refund status service on the portal.

Aditya, a Kochi-based content producer who keeps regular books, paid ₹1,50,000 of advance tax for tax year 2026-27. His final tax is ₹1,20,000, giving a refund of ₹30,000, which is 25% of his tax and so eligible for interest.

body.title: Try It: Refund Interest on Time
body.prompt: Shalini, a Chandigarh-based architect, has a refund of ₹48,000 against tax of ₹2,40,000 for tax year 2026-27. She files on time, and the refund is granted in November 2027. How much interest does she receive on the refund? Answer in rupees.
body.explanation: The refund is 20% of her tax, above the 10% minimum. From 1 April to November 2027 is 8 months, counting November in full. ₹48,000 × 0.5% × 8 = ₹1,920. That interest is taxable in the year she receives it.

children.text: Some taxpayers deliberately overpay advance tax to avoid any chance of interest. It works, but at a cost. Suppose you pay ₹1,00,000 more than needed on 15 June 2026 and get it back with the refund on 30 September 2027, about 15 months later.

body.title: What ₹1,00,000 earns from June 2026 to September 2027

data.label: Excess advance tax, refunded with interest

body.text: The refund interest of ₹3,000 covers only April to September 2027, because it starts on 1 April. Spread over the full 15 months your money was away, that is an effective return of about 2.3% a year, and the interest is taxable. A slightly high estimate is sensible insurance; a large deliberate overpayment is an expensive habit.

A refund can shrink before it reaches you. If the department shows an outstanding demand against you for an earlier year, it can adjust your refund against that demand after sending you an intimation and giving you a chance to respond. Check the outstanding demand section on the portal, and respond to any such intimation promptly if you disagree.

body.title: Scenario: Rakhi's Missing Refund
body.scenario: Rakhi, a freelance translator in Guwahati, filed her return for tax year 2026-27 on time in July 2027, claiming a refund of ₹36,000. In October the portal shows her return as processed with the refund determined, but no money has arrived. The refund status shows "refund failed". She changed banks in 2027 and closed the account listed in her old profile.
body.prompt: What has probably happened, and what should Rakhi do to get her refund?
body.modelAnswer: The refund was almost certainly sent to her closed account, or to an account that was not pre-validated, and bounced. Refunds are credited only to pre-validated bank accounts linked to the PAN. She should log in to the e-filing portal, open My Bank Account under her profile, remove or deactivate the closed account, add her new account with the correct account number and IFSC, and pre-validate it. Once it shows as validated, she should go to Services and then Refund Reissue, create a refund reissue request for tax year 2026-27, select the validated account, and e-verify the request. The refund, with interest, will then be reissued. For the future, she should update and pre-validate her bank details on the portal before filing every return.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: Tax on Refund Interest
body.textWithBlank: Interest received on an income tax refund is taxable as income from ___ sources in the year it is received.
body.explanation: Refund interest falls under income from other sources, taxed at your slab rate in the year you receive it. The refund itself is not income, because it is simply your own tax being returned.

body.title: Refund Readiness Checklist
steps: Before filing, pre-validate the bank account you want the refund in, under My Bank Account on the e-filing portal
Claim every TDS, TCS and advance tax credit exactly as it appears in AIS and Form 26AS
File by the due date so refund interest runs from 1 April
e-Verify the return the same day
Check the processing intimation for the refund and interest computed, and for any adjustment against old demands
If the refund fails, fix the bank account and raise a refund reissue request rather than waiting
Include refund interest received as income in the next return

cards.definition: The excess of TDS, TCS, advance tax and self-assessment tax over tax payable, paid out after your return is processed.
0.5% a month on refunds of 10% or more of tax, from 1 April if filed on time, or from the date of filing for belated returns. Old section 244A.
A return filed after the due date. It carries a late fee and loses refund interest for the period before filing.
A bank account verified on the e-filing portal. Refunds are credited only to such accounts.
A portal service to request a failed refund be sent again, usually after fixing the bank account.
The department may set off a refund against tax outstanding for an earlier year, after intimating you.

points: Excess TDS, TCS or advance tax is refunded only after you file your return and it is processed
Refund interest is 0.5% a month, from 1 April if you file on time, or from the date of filing if you file late
No interest is paid if the refund is less than 10% of the tax determined
Refund interest is taxable as income from other sources
Deliberate overpayment earns far less than an FD, because interest does not run while the year is in progress
Pre-validate your bank account and e-verify promptly, or your refund may be delayed or fail

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax, legal or investment advice. References to section 244A are to the Income-tax Act, 1961 provision carried into the Income-tax Act, 2025. Interest examples are simplified and ignore periods of delay attributable to the taxpayer. Portal services and processing times reflect the position as understood at the time of writing. Verify current rules or consult a qualified chartered accountant before acting.
